title: Closed [e] — é, -er, -ez, -ed, et, les/des/mes (set 4)
sounds: les / des / mes / tes / ses / ces
focus: All of these make the closed [e]: lips spread, tongue high, a pure « ay » with no glide at the end. It's spelled é; -er, -ez and -ed at the end of a word (parler, chez, pied); the word « et »; and the short words les, des, mes, tes, ses, ces. Exceptions: in a few short words the -er is [ɛʁ] with the r pronounced (mer, fer, hiver, cher, hier), and « est » has the open [ɛ]. Québécois keeps é and è clearly apart, even at the end of a word (« parlé » vs « parlait »).

sentences.fr: En [é]t[é], nous allons au lac avec m[es] grands-parents.
sentences.en: In summer, we go to the lake with my grandparents.

sentences.fr: Le matin, on aime nag[er] [et] pêch[er].
sentences.en: In the morning, we like to swim and fish.

sentences.fr: Mon grand-père pr[é]pare d[es] sandwichs pour le dîn[er].
sentences.en: My grandfather makes sandwiches for lunch.

sentences.fr: L'après-midi, on regarde l[es] canards [et] l[es] h[é]rons.
sentences.en: In the afternoon, we watch the ducks and the herons.

sentences.fr: Le soir, on chante [et] on mange d[es] guimauves grill[é]es.
sentences.en: In the evening, we sing and eat toasted marshmallows.
